message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Series | Title | Year Published | Notes |
|--------|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter** | *Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone* (U.S. title: *Sorcerer’s Stone*) | 1997 | First book in the series; introduces Harry, Hogwarts, and the wizarding world. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets* | 1998 | Harry returns to school and faces the mystery of the Chamber. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban* | 1999 | Introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire* | 2000 | The Triwizard Tournament and the return of Voldemort. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix* | 2003 | Focuses on the formation of Dumbledore’s Army. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince* | 2005 | Explores Voldemort’s past and the Horcruxes. |
| | *Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows* | 2007 | The epic conclusion to the series. |
| **Cormoran Strike** (written as Robert Galbraith) | *The Cuckoo’s Calling* | 2013 | A detective novel featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike. |
| | *The Silkworm* | 2014 | Strike investigates a missing author. |
| | *Career of Evil* | 2015 | Strike confronts a dangerous adversary. |
| | *Lethal White* | 2018 | Strike deals with a murder case involving a former colleague. |
| | *Troubled Blood* | 2020 | Strike investigates a cold case from 1975. |
| **Other Works** | *The Casual Vacancy* | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel, a dark political drama set in a small town. |
| | *The Ickabog* | 2020 | A children’s fable published as a free online book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |
| | *The Ickabog* (hardcover) | 2021 | The same story released in print. |

These titles have been bestsellers worldwide, received critical acclaim, and have been adapted into major film and television productions.
